q: A user says 'the printer is broken'. What do you do first?
options: Ask what changed, when it last worked, and whether others are affected
why: Context narrows the cause cheaply. Most problems follow a change or affect only one machine.

q: Why record a warranty end date in the inventory?
options: So you can plan replacement or repair cover before it lapses
why: Knowing expiry dates lets you budget and act before a failure becomes expensive.

q: The log shows 30 failed logons for one account, then a successful logon from the same address. Best reading?
options: Possible takeover: check the account, reset it and see what it did afterwards
why: Many failures followed by a success from the same source is a classic password-guessing pattern. It is a lead to investigate.

q: When someone leaves, what should you do with their account on day one?
options: Disable it, reset the password and sign out sessions, then delete after the retention period
why: Disabling keeps data and evidence available while stopping access. Deleting first can destroy what you later need.

q: Why is RAID not a backup?
options: It protects against a disk failing, not against deletion, ransomware or a fire
why: RAID copies mistakes instantly. A backup is a separate, restorable copy, ideally off-site and tested.

q: A new 1 TB drive shows about 931 GB in the operating system. What explains it?
options: The maker counts in powers of 1000 and the OS in powers of 1024
The drive is partly reserved for backups
why: 1 TB is 10^12 bytes. Divided by 1024^3 that is about 931 GiB, which many systems label GB. Nothing is missing.

q: What is the decimal value of binary 01010111?
why: 64 + 16 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 87. Hex 57 is the same bits written compactly, which is why 57 is a tempting wrong answer.

q: What does chmod 640 on a file allow?
options: Owner read and write, group read, others nothing
Owner read only, others read and write
why: 6 = read+write for the owner, 4 = read for the group, 0 = nothing for others.

q: Which mode makes a shared directory sticky so users can only delete their own files?
why: The leading 1 is the sticky bit; 1777 or 1775 are typical. 175 has no special bit at all.

q: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs differ?
why: XOR means exclusive or: different inputs give 1. XNOR is the opposite.

q: A TCP test to a port says 'connection refused' instantly, but another port just times out. What does that suggest?
options: Both are blocked the same way
Refused means the host answered and nothing listens; a timeout suggests a firewall or no route
Refused means the firewall dropped it
A timeout means the service is running
why: A refusal comes from the host itself. A silent timeout usually means packets are dropped on the way or the host is unreachable.

q: Before running a command you found online on a production server, you should:
options: Understand what it does and try it on a test machine or with a dry run first
Run it as administrator to be safe
why: Commands like mirror-copy or delete flags can destroy data. Read it, test it, and keep a backup.

q: A PC gets 169.254.20.5 and cannot reach anything. What is the most likely cause?
options: It could not reach a DHCP server and gave itself an APIPA address
The subnet mask is too large
why: 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA. Check the link, the DHCP server and its scope.

q: A hard drive is clicking and the PC reports 'bootable device not found'. What comes first?
options: Back up what you can, then replace the drive
Format it to clear the errors
why: Clicking means mechanical failure. Protect the data before anything else.

q: In the SOHO malware removal order, what follows verifying the symptoms?
why: Isolate it first so it can't spread; remediate and educate later.

q: A backup copies only what changed since the last full backup. Which type is it?
why: Differential grows each day but restores with just the full and the latest differential; incremental needs the whole chain.

q: You find a script online that fixes your problem. What should you do before running it?
options: Run it as administrator so it works
Read it, test it away from production and back up first
Disable antivirus so it is not blocked
Run it at night so nobody notices
why: Scripts can introduce malware or change settings. Read, test, back up.

q: Which change type is for an urgent fix that cannot wait for the usual approval cycle?
why: Emergency changes are expedited but still documented and reviewed afterwards.

q: A headset's microphone doesn't work on a laptop, but it works on an old phone. What is the likely cause?
options: A CTIA versus OMTP wiring mismatch on the 4-contact plug
The laptop has no sound card
why: The two layouts swap the ground and microphone contacts. An adapter converts between them.

q: You run 'parted /dev/sdb mklabel gpt'. When does the change happen?
why: parted writes as you go, unlike fdisk which keeps changes in memory until w. mklabel replaces the whole partition table, so check the device name first.

q: A domain GPO sets a wallpaper and an OU GPO sets a different one. Neither is Enforced. Which applies to a computer in that OU?
why: Local, Site, Domain, then OUs: the last applied wins, so the more specific OU wins unless the domain GPO is Enforced.

q: Within one container two GPOs conflict. Which wins?
options: The one with the highest link order number
why: Link order 1 is applied last, so it has the highest precedence.

q: Why shouldn't an LDIF file contain userPassword: Summer2024?
options: The password sits in plain text in a file that gets copied and logged; use a hash
It must be base64 and that is enough
why: Anyone who sees the file sees the password. Base64 is encoding, not protection.

q: Why is RAID 5 with very large disks risky?
options: One read error during a long rebuild can lose the array
why: Single parity must read every other disk perfectly during the rebuild, and the more data, the likelier a read error.

q: Which backup scheme restores from the fewest sets in a week with a weekly full?
why: A differential restore needs the last full plus one differential; incrementals need the full plus every incremental since.

q: A user gets a 502 Bad Gateway. Where do you look first?
options: The server behind the proxy or load balancer
why: 502 means a gateway got an invalid reply from the upstream server, so check that upstream and the proxy's timeouts.

q: Does a load balancer by itself make a service highly available?
options: No; it is a single point of failure unless it is redundant and uses health checks
why: Without health checks it keeps sending traffic to a dead server, and one balancer is a single point of failure.

q: Which title is best for a support ticket?
options: Outlook crashes when opening PDF attachments (Windows 11)
why: It names the program, the symptom and the setting. The others do not say what is wrong or where.

q: You fix a problem by restarting the PC and do not know why it failed. What is the best closing note?
options: Restarted, works now; cause unknown, will raise a problem ticket if it returns
why: It is honest about the cause and tells the next person what to do if the problem comes back.

q: Why should you never write a password in a ticket?
options: Many people can read tickets and they are kept, so the password is exposed
It makes the ticket low priority
why: A ticket is a shared, stored record. Say you can give the password by phone if it is needed.

q: In a vSphere build, why give management, vMotion and storage traffic separate networks or VLANs?
options: They have different security and performance needs and should not interfere
why: Mixing traffic types lets heavy migration or storage traffic disturb management, and widens the blast radius of a problem.

q: Which is a sound way to choose a software tool?
options: Know your stack and gaps, shortlist, trial it, and plan how to get your data out
Pick whatever a vendor ranking says is first
why: Ratings are one input. A trial shows fit, and an exit plan avoids lock-in. Vendor-published rankings are not neutral.

q: An incremental backup stores...
options: Only files that are new or changed since the last backup
why: Unchanged files are already stored (identified by their fingerprint), so each backup costs only the changes.

q: A restore drill tells you...
options: How long recovery takes and how much recent work would be lost
why: It proves the restore works (recovery time) and shows the gap since the last backup (recovery point).

q: Before running an inventory agent on staff computers you should...
options: Read it, limit what it collects, and tell the owners
why: A trustworthy agent collects only what the inventory needs, is read before it is run, and is announced.
